steps.tx: A chronic systemic autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis primarily targeting diarthrodial synovial joints characterizes **rheumatoid arthritis**. Driven by autoreactive CD4 T-helper cells, B lymphocytes, and macrophages producing pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-1, IL-6), synovial tissue undergoes marked hyperplastic proliferation. This invasive fibrovascular granulation tissue, termed pannus, secretes matrix metalloproteinases that erode articular cartilage and subchondral bone. Patients present with symmetrical joint swelling, tenderness, and prolonged morning stiffness lasting over an hour that improves with physical activity.
steps.say: A chronic systemic autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis primarily targeting diarthrodial synovial joints characterizes rheumatoid arthritis. Driven by autoreactive T cells and macrophages producing cytokines, synovial tissue undergoes marked hyperplastic proliferation. This invasive tissue, termed pannus, secretes metalloproteinases that erode cartilage and bone. Patients present with symmetrical joint swelling, tenderness, and morning stiffness lasting over an hour.

steps.tx: Diagnostic serological testing evaluates circulating autoantibodies directed against self immunoglobulins and post-translationally modified peptides. The classic **rheumatoid factor** (RF) is an IgM autoantibody directed against the Fc portion of human IgG, present in seventy to eighty percent of patients. While sensitive, RF is non-specific, occurring in systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjögren syndrome, and chronic infections like hepatitis C. In contrast, antibodies targeting cyclic citrullinated peptides (anti-CCP) exhibit comparable sensitivity (75%) with exceptional specificity exceeding ninety-five percent, strongly predicting aggressive erosive joint destruction.
steps.say: Diagnostic serological testing evaluates circulating autoantibodies directed against self immunoglobulins and modified peptides. The classic rheumatoid factor is an IgM antibody targeting human IgG, present in seventy percent of patients. While sensitive, rheumatoid factor occurs in other autoimmune diseases and hepatitis C. In contrast, anti-CCP antibodies demonstrate exceptional specificity exceeding ninety-five percent, strongly predicting aggressive erosive joint destruction.

left.title: Rheumatoid Factor (IgM anti-IgG Fc)
points: Cross-reactive in SLE, Sjögren, Hepatitis C
Can be negative in early disease (seronegative RA)

right.title: Anti-CCP / ACPA Antibodies
points: Detectable years prior to clinical arthritis
Strongest predictor of radiographic joint erosion

steps.tx: Modern diagnostic classification emphasizes early identification of inflammatory synovitis before irreversible bony erosions develop. Under the **acr/eular criteria** (2010), patients presenting with at least one joint displaying definite clinical synovitis not explained by another diagnosis are scored across four domains: joint involvement (up to 5 points for small joints), serology (RF or anti-CCP up to 3 points), acute-phase reactants (elevated CRP or ESR earns 1 point), and symptom duration (>= 6 weeks earns 1 point). Achieving a composite score of six or more out of ten confirms rheumatoid arthritis.
steps.say: Modern diagnostic classification emphasizes early identification of inflammatory synovitis before irreversible bony erosions develop. Under the ACR/EULAR criteria, patients presenting with definite clinical synovitis are scored across four domains: joint involvement, serology, acute-phase reactants, and symptom duration. Achieving a composite score of six or more out of ten confirms rheumatoid arthritis, mandating prompt initiation of disease-modifying antirheumatic therapy.

Duration of synovitis < 6 weeks (0 pt) vs >= 6 weeks (1 pt)

steps.tx: Chronic synovial proliferation stretching extensor tendons, collateral ligaments, and volar plates produces characteristic late hand deformities. In **swan neck deformity**, contracture of intrinsic hand muscles combined with volar plate stretching produces hyperextension of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint paired with compensatory flexion of the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint. Conversely, boutonnière deformity features rupture or attenuation of the central slip of the extensor digitorum tendon, allowing lateral bands to slip volarly and producing fixed flexion of the PIP joint with hyperextension of the DIP joint.
steps.say: Chronic synovial proliferation stretching extensor tendons, collateral ligaments, and volar plates produces characteristic late hand deformities. In swan neck deformity, contracture of intrinsic hand muscles produces hyperextension of the proximal interphalangeal joint with flexion of the distal interphalangeal joint. Conversely, boutonniere deformity features central extensor tendon rupture, producing flexion of the proximal interphalangeal joint with hyperextension of the distal joint.

right.title: Boutonnière Deformity

steps.tx: Progressive destruction of the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint capsules and collateral ligaments by aggressive synovial pannus produces characteristic angular malalignment. Chronic volar subluxation and extensor digitorum tendon slippage toward the ulnar side results in pronounced **ulnar deviation** of the digits at the MCP joints. Additionally, radial deviation of the carpal bones at the wrist creates the classic zigzag deformity of the rheumatoid hand. Early aggressive initiation of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) halts destructive synovitis, effectively preventing these disfiguring permanent mechanical deformities.

steps.tx: A potentially fatal neurological complication arises from synovial pannus erosion of the transverse atlantal ligament in the upper cervical spine. In **atlantoaxial subluxation**, synovial inflammation between the atlas (C1) and odontoid peg (axis, C2) erodes the transverse ligament, allowing the atlas to shift anteriorly during neck flexion. Severe subluxation risks catastrophic spinal cord compression, spastic quadriparesis, and sudden respiratory arrest. Patients report occipital neck pain and radiating paresthesias; lateral cervical spine radiographs in full flexion showing an anterior atlantodental interval exceeding three millimetres establish the diagnosis.
steps.say: A potentially fatal neurological complication arises from synovial pannus erosion of the transverse atlantal ligament in the upper cervical spine. In atlantoaxial subluxation, synovial inflammation erodes the transverse ligament, allowing the atlas to shift anteriorly during neck flexion. Severe subluxation risks spinal cord compression, quadriparesis, and sudden respiratory arrest. steps.tx: Systemic rheumatoid disease extends beyond articular structures to cause diverse extra-articular manifestations in seropositive patients. Firm, non-tender subcutaneous **rheumatoid nodules** develop in twenty to thirty percent of patients, characteristically localized over extensor pressure surfaces like the olecranon process, Achilles tendon, and bridge of the nose. Histologically, nodules exhibit central fibrinoid necrosis encircled by palisading epithelioid histiocytes. Other extra-articular manifestations include secondary keratoconjunctivitis sicca (secondary Sjögren syndrome), episcleritis, scleromalacia perforans, rheumatoid vasculitis with digital gangrene, and accelerated atherosclerotic coronary artery disease.

steps.tx: Establishing a treat-to-target strategy utilizing conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs immediately upon diagnosis achieves sustained clinical remission. Oral **methotrexate** represents the universal first-line anchor DMARD, acting as a competitive folate antagonist that inhibits dihydrofolate reductase and promotes adenosine release at inflammatory sites. Administering folic acid co-prescription mitigates methotrexate-induced stomatitis, nausea, and hepatotoxicity. If moderate-to-high disease activity persists after three to six months despite optimized methotrexate, biologic DMARDs (TNF inhibitors, IL-6 receptor antagonists) or targeted synthetic JAK inhibitors are added.
steps.say: Establishing a treat-to-target strategy utilizing conventional disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs immediately upon diagnosis achieves sustained clinical remission. Oral methotrexate represents the universal first-line anchor therapy, acting as a folate antagonist that promotes extracellular adenosine release. Administering folic acid mitigates stomatitis, nausea, and liver enzyme elevations. If high disease activity persists despite methotrexate, biologic therapies or targeted synthetic JAK inhibitors are added.

nodes.label: First-Line Anchor: Oral Methotrexate (15-25 mg/wk) + Folic Acid
Assess CDAI / DAS28 at 3 Months (Treat to Target)
If Target Not Met: Add Biologic DMARD (TNF / IL-6) or JAK Inhibitor
